title: Course & Curriculum Planner
description: Instructors and course designers: plan units, lessons and outcomes with pacing.

spec.useCase: Corinne Delacroix coordinates curriculum at a small college and uses this to see pacing, readiness and outcome coverage for every course.

business.name: Meadowlark Academy
business.describes: A small college offering evening and weekend courses.

tables.name: Courses
tables.describes: Each course with its level, instructor, dates and how many units and lessons it has.
tables.subject: thing

independentOf.instructor: Any instructor can lead a course whenever they joined.

tables.name: Units
tables.describes: Each unit of a course, its order and dates, with the lesson time and progress rolled up.
tables.subject: thing

independentOf.course: A unit may start a little before or after the course dates when the schedule moves.

question.whyItMatters: Corinne checks that drafts are ready a week before they run.

text.text: Map a course from outcomes to units to lessons. Plan the pacing on the timeline, then mark lessons Ready and Complete as the term runs.
Open the Year at a glance page for every course on one timeline.
Read the Course progress figure alongside the timeline. If progress trails the calendar, trim a lesson rather than rushing every lesson.
Timeline shows course and unit spans; look for months with no teaching.
Assessments list shows when marking lands; spread them so two never fall in one week.
Compare Course progress to the calendar every month.
Work through this once per course.
Write four to eight outcomes in plain language.
Split the term into three to six units with dates.
Add lessons to each unit, then link each to the outcomes it covers.
Check that every outcome is covered by at least one lesson and one assessment.
Mark lessons Ready once materials are prepared.
An outcome with zero lessons covering it is a gap. Fix the plan before the term starts.
Plan the assessment first and the lessons backwards from it.
